newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsubishi Motors, Volvo to strengthen tie-up.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi Motors, Volvo to strengthen tie-up.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Tuesday that it and AB Volvo had agreed to strengthen their tie-up.

A Mitsubishi spokesman said the two companies will consider jointly selling commercial vehicles in Europe. They will also consider sharing car components globally and developing a new engine, he said.
"They are broad directions and details will need to be discussed," the Mitsubishi spokesman said.
The agreement was made in order to strengthen the two companies' competitiveness, he said.
Mitsubishi and Volvo currently produce cars at their Dutch joint venture NedCar, which is equally owned by them and the Dutch government.

The agreement was made last weekend between Mitsubishi chairman Hirokazu Nakamura and top Volvo executives including the chief executive officer of Volvo's car division Volvo Car, Tuve Johannesson, another Mitsubishi Motors spokesman said.

The spokesman said that Mitsubishi was likely to supply Volvo's passenger car division with the technology for its newly developed gasoline direct injection (GDI) engine. The GDI engine is a fuel-efficient engine that Mitsubishi says considerably cuts carbon dioxide emissions.
Mitsubishi Motors said in Ocotober it would supply its gasoline direct injection (GDI) engines in the future for AB Volvo cars made at the NedCar joint venture.
Mitsubishi Motors also said in October that the Japanese-made engine will be used in S40 and V40 cars which Volvo produces at NedCar in the Netherlands.
Under the agreement made last weekend, Volvo's truck unit will supply heavy trucks in the future to Mitsubishi's sales network in Asian countries, the spokesman said.
